Subject: Follow-up: Redwood demo & token economics

Vanessa / Karthik — thanks again for the demo today, that was helpful. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying Qs so you can propose options.

Recap / rough baseline:
- App: Prose AI editor (SaaS). Peak workload: ~180 rps in a single region, steady-state 40–60 rps.
- Typical request: 180 tokens input + 230 tokens generated on average => ~410 tokens/request.
- Expected monthly volume for initial rollout: ~45M requests => ~18.45B tokens/month. (We understand these are approximate; happy to refine.)
- Latency target: p50 <= 250ms for text generation on interactive editor; p95 ideally < 800ms.
- Current budget range for inference: $15k–$30k / month for MVP.
- Preference: start on hosted but evaluate dedicated if unit economics improve.

Questions for your quote:
1) For the volumes above, what are the expected $ / 1M tokens for Hosted standard vs Hosted low-latency (streaming) vs Dedicated (monthly commit)?
2) How much incremental latency reduction do we get from streaming + smaller batch sizes? Any recommended SLO-driven pricing tiers?
3) If we commit to a 6–12 month reserved pool, what kind of per-token uplift vs pay-as-you-go should we assume?

Happy to jump on a short call tomorrow if that helps. Attaching our high-level traffic spreadsheet in a follow-up (will send raw numbers).

Thanks,
Alex

Alex — great to connect earlier. Thanks for the clear numbers — that helps a lot. I put together a short options matrix and a basic token-econ model (attached) to illustrate trade-offs. Attachment: redwood-token-econ-model.xlsx (estimates only).

Top-line answers and clarifying Qs: 
- Quick answers (high level):
  • Hosted standard (pay-as-you-go): $700–$850 per 1M tokens at your volume band (est.) — p50 ~350–500ms depending on model choice and burst.
  • Hosted streaming (low-latency config, smaller batches): $1,100–$1,350 per 1M tokens — typically gets p50 down to ~150–300ms but increases unit cost.
  • Dedicated reserved pool (6–12mo commit): $420–$620 per 1M tokens (effective, depends on commit size + concurrency). Latency typically similar to streaming if you provision for low-queueing (config + instance type matter).

- Key assumptions I used in the spreadsheet: model = open-llama-70B (quantized), avg tokens/request = 410, sustained concurrency 40–60 rps, peak 180 rps burst; batching behavior assumed 8–16 token-group batching for standard, 1–4 for streaming.

- Clarifying Qs for accuracy:
  1) Can you confirm whether the 180 rps peak is single-region only? (we assumed yes)
  2) Are you comfortable with an initial model choice in the open family, or do you need a specific proprietary model?
  3) Would you like us to include a plan with KV/prefix caching and a small-edge cache for repeated prompts? That can materially lower token counts for editing flows.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll draft three concrete pricing scenarios in a separate email (hosted payg, hosted streaming SLO tier, and 6-mo dedicated commit) with explicit $/1M and expected latency bands.
2) If any of those look good, we can spin up a 2-week hosted streaming trial (no commit) to measure real p50/p95 with your workload.
3) If you prefer to optimize for cost, we’ll model a dedicated reserve and show the break-even month.

I’ll run this by our pricing lead (cc’d: Karthik) and loop in Rishi from infra for any infra-specific notes. Expect a follow-up with concrete numbers by EOD tomorrow.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Exec | Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>

Subject: INTERNAL: Prose AI — model/latency trade-offs + suggested quotes

Internal note — copying the key points from Alex and my initial numbers. Please keep this internal; we will publish the customer-facing breakdown after we align.

Customer baseline: 18.45B tokens / month (est), p50 target 250ms, p95 <800ms, budget $15–30k/mo. Wants hosted to start.

Options to model (we should include three scenarios + sensitivity):
- Scenario A (Cost-opt): Hosted standard, batching optimized for throughput, prefix caching on repeated editor prompts. Assumptions: batching factor 8–12, avg latency p50 ~350–500ms. Nominal $/1M = $700–$850. Notes: good for cost but p95 will vary on bursts.
- Scenario B (Latency-first / streaming): Hosted streaming or high-priority queue, minimal batching (1–4), early token flush, plus streaming to client. Nominal $/1M = $1,100–$1,350. p50 ~150–300ms; p95 improved but more sensitive to network.
- Scenario C (Reserved commit / Dedicated): 6–12 month commit, reserved GPU pools sized for peak, targeted batching small if pinned to low-latency lanes. Effective $/1M = $420–$620 depending on commit. Latency comparable to B if we reserve capacity appropriately.

Pricing mechanics we should confirm:
- Whether to offer an SLO-driven premium (e.g., +40–80% on base $/1M for an SLO-backed low-latency tier) vs a managed low-latency product. This helps customers trade cost vs guaranteed latency.
- How to present burst credits and overage on dedicated pools.

Quick asks for Rishi: do we have example perf profiles (p50/p95) for the model family at 40–60 sustained rps and 180 rps burst for the planned instance types? Also need a sanity check on the dedicated effective $/1M math at 18B tokens/mo after amortizing reserved infra and maintenance.

Karthik — if you can draft the customer-facing numbers (table + short narrative) I’ll review and send.

-Vanessa
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Alex — following up with three concrete scenarios based on the assumptions Vanessa shared. These are estimates; we can run a short trial to validate.

Summary table (estimates):
1) Hosted — throughput-optimized (payg)
  • Estimated $ / 1M tokens: $760
  • Expected latency: p50 350–500ms; p95 700–1,200ms
  • Pros: lowest onboarding friction, no commit.
  • Cons: higher tail latency on bursts; batching can add queuing.

2) Hosted — streaming / SLO tier (low-latency)
  • Estimated $ / 1M tokens: $1,220
  • Expected latency: p50 160–280ms; p95 450–700ms
  • Pros: best interactive experience; streaming reduces perceived latency.
  • Cons: ~60% higher unit cost vs standard.

3) Dedicated — 6 mo reserve (recommended if you need predictable unit cost)
  • Estimated $ / 1M tokens: $510 (with a 6-mo commit sized for your peaks)
  • Expected latency: p50 150–300ms; p95 depends on provisioning buffers
  • Pros: best long-term unit economics; control over autoscale and capacity lanes.

Additional notes:
- Break-even analysis: at your projected 18.45B tokens/mo, Dedicated becomes cost-effective vs Hosted streaming in ~1.5–3 months depending on commit sizing and eligible discounts. The attached spreadsheet (shared by Vanessa) has the math.
- Streaming reduces average latency by avoiding multi-request batching and flushing tokens earlier to the client; it increases compute overhead because models are less batchable.
- We recommend a two-week hosted streaming pilot instrumented with p50/p95 traces and token-level cost breakdown. That will give a realistic comparison before any commit.

Proposed next steps:
1) Kick off the 2-week hosted streaming pilot (no commit) — Redwood to provide pilot keys and a simple dashboard.
2) After pilot, review metrics and either (a) move to 6-mo Dedicated reserve (preferred if cost math checks) or (b) stay on Hosted SLO tier.

Would Thursday 10am PT for a short sync to kick off pilot work for your engineers work?

Best,
Karthik Iyer
